question: A test class has `private int counter = 0;` and two tests that each run `counter++` and then assert `counter == 1`. Both pass in any order. Why?
options: JUnit resets all fields by reflection after each test
JUnit creates a new instance of the class for every test method
The tests run in parallel on separate machines
Fields in test classes are automatically final
explanation: The default lifecycle is per method: a new instance for each test, so instance state never carries over. PER_CLASS would share one instance.

question: A test calls `assertEquals` four times for four fee amounts, and the first one fails. What do you see for the other three?
options: Their results are reported too
Nothing: the test method stopped at the first failing assertion
They are retried automatically
They are reported as skipped
explanation: A failing assertion throws immediately. Wrapping the four checks in assertAll runs all of them and lists every failure together.

question: You must verify that a method throws and that the message contains the offending value. Which approach does both?
options: Wrap the call in try/catch and ignore the catch block
Annotate the test with `@Disabled`
Call the method twice and compare the results
Use `assertThrows` and assert on the message of the returned exception
explanation: assertThrows fails if nothing is thrown and returns the exception, so you can check getMessage. A try/catch with an empty catch passes even when nothing is thrown.

question: A fee rule changes at 40 days. Which set of parameterized inputs best protects the rule?
explanation: Bugs cluster at boundaries. Values just below, at and just above the change catch off-by-one mistakes that values far from it never reach.

question: When must a `@BeforeAll` method be static?
options: Never: it must always be an instance method
Always, in every test class
In the default per-method lifecycle, because no instance exists yet; PER_CLASS lifts the rule
Only inside nested classes
explanation: With the default lifecycle the method runs before any instance exists, so it must be static. @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) creates one instance first and allows non-static methods.

question: A build should run all tests except those labeled `slow` on every commit. Which setup does that?
options: Rename the slow tests to start with an underscore
Put them in a nested class
Mark them with `@Tag("slow")` and exclude the group, for example with `-DexcludedGroups=slow`
Remove their assertions
explanation: Tags label tests, and Surefire can include or exclude groups by tag. Renaming or nesting does not filter anything.
